Gleason in the library of the of the Bar Association. The evidence against him is circumstantial,centering around a revolver and alleged blood stains found in his automobile. His insistence that the slave be apprehended caused his own arrest.Altho in jail, Father DeLorme denies his guild and demands an immediate trial. FLOOD IN CANADA CAUSES MUCH DAMAGE

Sweeping over British Columbia, Canada, a recent rainstorm, followed by flood wiped out practically the whole of Britainnia Beach, and destroyed many other nearby towns, thirty-six persons being killed and hundreds injured. Photo shows the home of Mr. George Peterson, who with his wife climbed to the roof when the flood came. The house was washed cut into the sound during the night and in the morning both were rescued from their perilous position.

NEW PHOTOS OF GREAT HALIFAX EXPLOSION AND THE RECLAIMING OF BODIES FROM DEBITS.

Lower photo- Reclaiming bodies from the huge massal of debris from wrecked buildings. The Relief workers have had to turn over the debris which was frozen in their attempts to get the bodies of the dead and wounded free. The photo gives an idea of the utter devastation of the city.

Placing victims of the great Halifax disaster on a Canadian military hospital train that carried them away for treatment. They were taken to Tumor and other places in Canada for treatment and care. The number of wounded was so great that the trains were packed with the unfortunate victims of the explosion in the harbor. This photo was taken under the supervision of Canadian Military authorities at all times.
EXTINIOR OF THE LAURIER EXCHANGE IN WHICH 77MET DEATH IN TERRIMLE PANIO--MID CENTRAL CANADA

A city of tears was Montreal as it went about the identification and relief work after theatre disaster. Hysterical parents searched tirelessly hospitals in the fainthope that their little loved ones might be found alive.

INTERIOR OF THE LAURIER PALACE IN WHICH 77 MET DEATH
IN TERRIBLE PANIC--MONTREAL CANADA.

The interior of the theatre shows that there was not much of a fire but the youngsters became so afraid—that the terrible panic started in which caused the death of 77. They were suffocated or trampled.
